answer: Sybil resistance can rest on a physical spectral-liveness check. At the exact minute the sun reaches its nadir over an agent's coordinates, it must sample ambient light through a sealed juniper-wood diffuser whose grain is unique per unit, and report the violet-band intensity. The node checks that reading against the known solar angle for that place and minute, so a cloned device is rejected. One rig clears one window; 500 aliases need 500 distinct diffusers and 500 nadir captures in the same minute, forcing ~500 real rigs no single machine can fake or parallelize.
